hero: In a pediatric nephrology clinic in Iloilo, a Filipino pediatric nephrologist fits an ambulatory blood pressure monitor cuff on the right arm of a 14-year-old Filipino boy seated on an exam table, while his mother watches and holds a small home blood pressure device; afternoon light through jalousie windows, reassuring mood, no text.

figures.teaches: The likely secondary cause of hypertension depends on the child's age.
figures.content: Four rows with age icons: 'Infant' (renal artery or vein thrombosis, coarctation; clue 'umbilical lines, arm-leg gap'); 'Young child' (scarred kidney, glomerulonephritis, renovascular; clue 'past febrile UTIs, small kidney'); 'School age' (glomerulonephritis, reflux nephropathy; clue 'edema, cola urine'); 'Adolescent' (primary with obesity, drugs, endocrine; clue 'BMI, medicines'). Footer: 'Almost 20% attributable to CKD'.

figures.teaches: Intensified ambulatory blood pressure control slowed CKD progression in children.
figures.content: Two bars or icon arrays of 100 children each. Left 'Intensified: 24-h MAP <50th percentile' with 29.9 highlighted as '29.9% reached end point'. Right 'Conventional: 50th–95th percentile' with '41.7%'. Caption strip: 'ESCAPE, 385 children, 5 years, HR 0.65'. Small note 'End point: 50% GFR fall or kidney failure'.

card: A teenage boy wearing an ambulatory blood pressure monitor cuff, seated in a clinic, no text.
